subject: Parallelization of micro_ncep() for a great number of points across a landscape

messages.author: 15914ff4afa133aa
messages.subject: Parallelization of micro_ncep() for a great number of points across a landscape
parts:
Hey all,

I have a fair few number of spatial points (650+) that I want to get a time series of relevant micro-climatic data for. I have access to a machine with a high core count, adequate RAM, and stable internet connection and figured it would be an ideal situation for setting up runs in parallel. I am attempting to do so with the foreach package after setting up a local cluster. The model works fine for running points sequentially, but when when I try and run in parallel I seems to get problems with the forcing data being saved locally somewhere in the process, which causes read/write issues for each process as the forcing data are not uniquely named. Would a solution to this be setting up separate working directories for each worker but having the outputs save to a master file?  Any other thoughts on solutions?

Best,
Andrew

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Parallelization of micro_ncep() for a great number of points across a landscape
parts:
Hi Andrew,

The model shouldn't be writing unless you set the 'write_input' or 'writecsv' parameters as non-zero, or in the micro_ncep function having 'save' not equal to zero. Perhaps you need to change these settings in your simulation?

Also, you might consider downloading local copies of the gridded data for this kind of problem. You can then set the 'opendap' parameter to 0 (in micro_usa or micro_ncep) and specify the local folder location of the gridded data with the input 'spatial'.

All the best,
Mike
